00:00 Speaker 1: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Morgan from Redwood. do we have everyone on the line?
00:05 Dana Ortiz: yes this is Dana, hi Morgan. Liam and Priya are here as well.
00:09 Speaker 2: great, i think the agenda is short - cost/unit economics first, then deployment options, then next steps. sound good?
00:18 Liam Chen: yep, main thing for us is budget predictability. we're looking at roughly $25k a month cap for inference for a first-year pilot. need to understand per-token math and how batching/caching could move that.
00:30 Samir Patel: perfect. quick high level - Redwood offers Hosted (per-token), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC / on-prem). the unit economics change based on batching, cache hit rate, and model quantization. would you share the typical request profile?
00:47 Dana Ortiz: sure. our inference is a user-facing assistant: avg prompt+response 600 tokens, p50 latency preference <100ms, p95 ideally <250ms. peak qps ~25, sustained qps ~10. we also do nightly batch embeddings for indexing but that's off-peak.
01:05 Samir Patel: ok that's helpful. so rough math: for Hosted we price per input and output token; with continuous batching you can reduce per-token GPU time if requests arrive concurrently. caching - prefix or KV cache - can cut repeated context cost by 20-60% depending on reuse. quantized model variants (8-bit/4-bit) reduce GPU memory and cost but there is small quality delta.
01:28 Priya Rao: what about latency tradeoffs when you batch? we can't sacrifice p50 too much.
01:33 Samir Patel: right, batching increases throughput but can add a small scheduling delay. Redwood does adaptive batching: we set a micro-batch window (e.g., 10-30ms) and dynamic sizing so p50 is largely unchanged, p95 can be impacted if you push for higher throughput. Dedicated gives you more control - you get reserved capacity, lower scheduling jitter.
01:50 Dana Ortiz: can you give a simple per-token example? numbers are helpful for our finance folks.
01:55 Morgan Lee: absolutely. for Hosted nominal model (let's say a 70B open model) our list price is X cents per 1k input tokens and Y cents per 1k output tokens - (note: numbers discussed verbally, we'll send exact sheet) - but practically, with batching and a 30% cache hit rate, your effective per-token cost can drop by ~25-35% compared to naive per-token math. with Dedicated, if you commit to a reserved pool you can see ~30-50% lower unit cost depending on utilization and model fits.
02:22 Liam Chen: hmm okay. our usage profile has spiky daytime traffic so burst capacity is important. does Dedicated support burst to hosted?
02:28 Samir Patel: yes - we offer configurable burst tiers. you can reserve a baseline and then allow overflow to Hosted for spikes, with fallback policies to cheaper model variants if capacity is constrained. that helps keep latency during spikes but you pay the hosted rates for overflow.
02:45 Priya Rao: on Private deployments, what's the main difference on cost? we prefer VPC for data controls but worried about ops overhead.
02:51 Samir Patel: Private gives you the control and integration with your KMS and network egress policies. unit cost will depend on where you run (cloud region, on-prem hardware). you remove our hosted margins but you take on infra and ops costs; Redwood's Private can be deployed with a managed-control-plane model to reduce ops. we'll work with your infra team to estimate.
03:09 Dana Ortiz: security stuff - we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration. do you have docs?
03:15 Morgan Lee: yes we'll share our security whitepaper and SOC2 report. Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations, and we expose audit logs for all inference requests.
03:23 Dana Ortiz: great. for the bench, what do you need from us?
03:26 Samir Patel: a representative trace or sample of request payloads, and a small dataset to run 24-48 hour benchmarks: we run latency and cost-per-unit measurements across Hosted and Dedicated and share a workbook with token breakdowns. we also test cache hit simulations.
03:41 Liam Chen: can you simulate different cache hit rates? our assistant does long-lived contexts, so hope for high prefix reuse.
03:47 Samir Patel: yes - we'll parameterize bench runs at 0%, 30%, 60% cache reuse and show cost delta and latency impact.
03:55 Dana Ortiz: on pricing, do you do committed discounts for Dedicated monthly commits?
03:59 Morgan Lee: yes, committed monthly or annual pricing with volume tiers; committed capacity reduces per-token equivalent cost significantly. also we can model predictive utilization to show break-even vs Hosted.
04:12 Priya Rao: anything about multi-region routing? we need EU data residency for some users.
04:16 Samir Patel: we support region pinning for Hosted and Dedicated; Private obviously under your control. we can route EU traffic to EU clusters and apply residency controls in policies.
04:26 Dana Ortiz: customers sometimes worry about transcription - sorry i mean transcription of logs? are logs PII? how do you handle redaction?
04:33 Morgan Lee: good question. logs are configurable: you can disable request/response logging, redact PII, and we support field-level redaction. it's in the security docs we'll share.
04:42 Liam Chen: competitor question: we already have some stuff in Anthropic and also eval'd Bedrock. how do you compare on unit cost?
04:48 Morgan Lee: rough comparative - public LLM APIs often have simpler pricing but less control to optimize batching/caching at infra level. Bedrock is useful but cost-to-performance depends on your exact model; with Dedicated and caching, many customers see 20-40% better unit economics over time. we'll include comparative scenarios in the pricing workbook.
05:05 Dana Ortiz: ok next steps?
05:08 Morgan Lee: i'll send the tailored pricing sheet and security docs by EOD tomorrow. Samir will run a bench once you share traces - we aim for a 48-hour run next week. Dana, you suggested a pilot kickoff?
05:17 Dana Ortiz: yes, let's schedule the pilot kickoff for next Wednesday.
05:21 Liam Chen: fine. one more quick - SLA on latency and uptime for Dedicated?
05:25 Samir Patel: Dedicated has SLA-backed throughput and latency targets; we can discuss exact numbers in the SOW.
05:31 Dana Ortiz: thanks all.
05:33 Speaker 1: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and schedule.
